title: Python: a resolved from-import or module-attribute call must read m's module-level bindings, not its symbol table (DEC-303 (a43) item 2)
description: DEC-303 (a43) item 2, opum-ai/opum-doc#2010 (ODOC-640), 2026-11-26T10:25Z, verbatim: 'The module-binding gap is a DEFECT against rules in force, not a design question. resolveImportBinding and resolveModuleAttribute read m's symbol table rather than m's bindings. So in m.py, def f(): pass followed by del f or f = 1 still resolves from m import f; f() and m.f() to m.f, while ALIAS's module arm refuses g = m.f; g(). The rules in force already decide it, carried across the import: (a22) item 2: every module-level binding of the name counts, including writes through global in the same module. (a40) item 1: a del target is a binding. A non-def binding (an assignment of a non-def value, or a del) makes the name rebound. It is binned as a same-module bare-name call to a rebound name already is, with no edge to the def. Alternative defs or classes (platform arms, try/except fallbacks) keep (a10) Q2: one edge to every alternative, each flagged multiplyBound. No new rule is made. In particular, there is no rule that a def must be its names ONLY module-level binding, which would wrongly refuse (a10) Q2's alternatives. glyph-clis record-only filing becomes the fix task, with red/green fixtures for from-import and module-attribute calls after del and after reassignment, and an (a10) Q2 control that keeps its edges.' Found by the #180 round 1 review (F7); predates GCLI-115. HOLD STATUS: HELD as an invariant (DEC-303 (a46) item 6, opum-ai/opum-doc#2013, 2026-11-26T10:49Z): GCLI-116 lands before the analyzer freezes for the blind sample and joins (a36) item 1(i) alongside (a45) item 4. It was recorded NOT HELD by (a44) item 3; (a46) corrects that, because auto.tqdm has a non-resolving binding and the (a43) count missed edges that reach through the name. COUNT (glyph-cli, 2026-11-26, analyzer at opum-ai/glyph-cli#180 head e65fec1; resolved edges whose callee is a module-level def or class in another file, target name checked for non-def module-level bindings by python ast; read: flask 538, jinja 775, httpx 1042, rich 2981, tqdm 295 edges, no unparsed file): flask 0, jinja 0, httpx 0; rich 21 sites, all to rich/live.py:41 Live (from .live import Live as Live at line 307 under if __name__ == '__main__'); tqdm 11 sites: 9 to tqdm/utils.py:34 envwrap (from envwrap import envwrap at line 80, try/except ModuleNotFoundError after the def) and 2 to tqdm/auto.py:27 tqdm (tqdm = asyncio_tqdm at line 30, except branch). Total 32 sites on 3 names, of which 7 are package sites (rich/progress.py:1093, rich/spinner.py:130, rich/status.py:36, tqdm/contrib/discord.py:110, slack.py:71, telegram.py:107, tqdm/std.py:958). The count was of a wider set than (a43) item 2 defines (see the (a44) note). Build scope is the (a44) item 3 list, in the note and the acceptance criteria. The build comes after opum-ai/glyph-cli#180 lands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: red/green fixtures: m.py def f then del f, and def f then f = <value that does not resolve to a def or class>; from m import f; f() and import m; m.f() each resolve to no edge to m.f and are binned as a rebound bare-name call is (nothing on the pins moves)

rule (ii) across from-import and module-attribute resolution: alternative defs or classes of one name in m, or an import or assignment that resolves to a different def or class (platform arms, try/except fallbacks), give one edge to every alternative, each flagged multiplyBound and counted once as resolved-in-repo; an external alternative adds no in-repo edge
rule (i) control pinning rich/live.py's shape: an alternative that resolves to the SAME def or class keeps one edge with no multiplyBound flag
an unconditional later rebinding to a value that resolves (def f, then f = g, no branch) is pinned as rebound with no edge (a44 item 4, conservative reading)
global-write variant: def reset(): global f; f = <non-resolving value> or del f in m refuses the cross-module call too

the five-pin corpus diff is script-asserted with each moved site named; the two created tqdm/auto.py edges and any other in-repo edge created or removed on the pins come to opum-doc before the clear (a34, a40 item 2); the multiplyBound flag on the 9 envwrap sites is a flag change, not an edge change

implementationNotes: DEC-303 (a44), opum-ai/opum-doc#2011 (ODOC-640), 2026-11-26T10:29Z, verbatim: '1. Reading. In (a43) item 2, non-def binding means what that item says: a del, or an assignment of a value that does NOT resolve to a def or class under the rules in force. An import, or an assignment of a name that resolves to a def or class (in-repo or external), is not a non-def binding. It is an alternative binding of the name, and two rules decide it: (i) If the alternative resolves to the SAME def or class, it is no alternative. The site keeps one edge, with no multiplyBound flag. (ii) If it resolves to a DIFFERENT target, it follows (a10) Q2, carried across the import. The site gets one edge to every alternative, each flagged multiplyBound, and is counted once as resolved-in-repo. An external alternative is recorded as an external resolution is. It adds no in-repo edge. 2. Applied to the three names: rich/live.py:41 Live (21 sites): Rule (i) applies. The import at line 307, from .live import Live as Live under if __name__ == main, resolves to the same class, so the edges stand unchanged. No __main__ rule is made. tqdm/utils.py:34 envwrap (9 sites): Rule (ii) applies, with an external alternative. from envwrap import envwrap in the try after the def is a try/except fallback in Q2s own words. Each site keeps its edge to the in-repo def, now flagged multiplyBound. tqdm/auto.py:27 tqdm (2 sites): Rule (ii) applies, with an in-repo alternative. tqdm = asyncio_tqdm in the other branch resolves to the asyncio tqdm class. Each site gets an edge to both alternatives, each flagged multiplyBound. Those 2 created edges come to opum-doc before the clear, under (a40) item 2. 3. Hold: NOT held. Under this reading, zero sites on the pins have a binding that rebinds the name, so (a43) item 3 zero arm applies: GCLI-116 proceeds at normal priority and does not join (a36) item 1 hold. None of the 32 edges is wrong. The 11 tqdm sites lack the multiplyBound flag, and 2 of them also lack one alternative's edge. GCLI-116 builds: the del and non-resolving-value fixtures from (a43) item 2 (red/green; nothing on the pins moves); rule (ii) across from-import and module-attribute resolution; a rule (i) control, pinning rich/live.py shape. 4. Named, not ruled. An UNCONDITIONAL later rebinding at module level to a value that resolves (def f, then f = g, with no branch) is not on the pins. GCLI-116 pins it as rebound, with no edge, as the conservative reading. Whether last-binding-in-module-order (as A1 uses) should resolve it is not queued. glyph-cli may propose it the (a21) way, with development-corpus counts.' The earlier record of an OPEN hold and of the open reading question is superseded by this note.

BUILD (GO 2026-11-26). moduleBindingGate in src/python/calls.ts reads m's module-scope bindings (after the global and nonlocal redirects) for from-import and module-attribute calls; rules per (a43) item 2 and (a44). Open point sent to opum-doc: a conditional assignment whose value resolves to no def or class (tqdm/auto.py: tqdm = asyncio_tqdm, whose import does not resolve because tqdm/asyncio.py binds tqdm only by an alias) is built as contributing nothing (option A), so auto.tqdm stays the class; the ruled two-alternative edges there need cross-module single-alias resolution (option B), a separate ruling. Unconditional later rebinding (def f; f = g) is rebound with no edge (a44 item 4).

DEC-303 (a46), opum-ai/opum-doc#2013, 2026-11-26T10:49Z: (1) the (a44) item 2 line for tqdm/auto.py is CORRECTED: asyncio_tqdm does not resolve, so an assignment whose value does not resolve makes the name rebound, no edge; the gate as built is the ruled behaviour and the two created edges and the multiplyBound pair for auto.tqdm do not happen. (2) Neither A (a conditional alternative that does not resolve contributes nothing) nor B (single-alias resolution across the import) is taken; either may come as a recall proposal the (a21) way. (3) Removed edges are not yet accepted: reported by file, line and column, split package, tests and examples; none is among the labelled tqdm sample sites of test/python-dev-measurement/labels-tqdm.json. (4) Fixtures: a def in one arm with a non-resolving assignment in the other refuses in the cross-module from-import, the module-attribute and the same-module bare-name call. (5) rich/console.py:566:33 to _windows.py:40 accepted under (a10) Q2. (6) The hold is an invariant, recorded in the description.
